2607.29066.title: Semantics of Subterfuge: Benchmarking Legal Deception Detection Against General-domain State-of-the-Art
2607.29066.paper_summary: Deception detection has critical implications for legal proceedings, law enforcement, and online security. Although human judgment is limited in accuracy and scalability, Natural Language Processing (NLP) offers a data-driven alternative. We present a survey and comparative analysis of NLP-based Automatic Deception Detection (ADD) focusing on the legal domain, reviewing the evolution from feature-based machine learning to Large Language Model (LLM) approaches. We conduct a unified empirical evaluation across seven datasets (two legal, five general-domain), comparing six fine-tuned transformer models and seven LLMs under four prompting strategies. The results show strong domain sensitivity, with fine-tuned models excelling in data-rich general domains and few-shot LLMs remaining competitive in low-resource legal settings. Chain-of-Thought prompting often underperforms direct classification. These findings highlight the need for domain adaptation and interpretable systems in high-stakes legal contexts.
2607.29066.paper_summary_zh: 欺騙檢測對法律程序、執法和網絡安全具有重要的影響。雖然人類判斷的準確性和可擴展性有限，自然語言處理（NLP）提供了一種數據驅動的替代方案。我們提出了一項針對法律領域的基於NLP的自動欺騙檢測（ADD）的調查和比較分析，回顧了從基於特徵的機器學習到大型語言模型（LLM）方法的演變。我們在七個數據集（兩個法律數據集，五個通用領域數據集）上進行了統一的實證評估，比較了六個經過微調的Transformer模型和七個LLM在四種提示策略下的表現。結果顯示出強烈的領域敏感性，經過微調的模型在數據豐富的通用領域表現優異，而少量樣本的LLM在資源匱乏的法律環境中仍然具有競爭力。思維鏈提示通常表現不如直接分類。這些發現突顯了在高風險法律環境中對領域適應和可解釋系統的需求。
